description: Re-run of the identical deterministic node_budget=0 walkthrough that previously produced SIMULATED/SIMULATION from Grok (see 2026-09-26_grok_hypothetical_deterministic_simulated.json), run AFTER the EVIDENCE_CLASS_INSTRUCTIONS clarification was added to kernel.py/adapters.py explicitly distinguishing INFERRED (deterministic trace through a known rule) from SIMULATED (modeling a stochastic/underspecified process forward). Tests whether the documentation fix actually changes Grok's behavior on the same input.

seed_claim.content: project() builds a must-keep set starting from active seed_ids, then walks DEPENDS_ON/CONTRADICTS relations to unconditionally add hinge claims to that set. If the resulting must-keep set size exceeds node_budget, project() returns INSUFFICIENT_PROJECTION and no claims or relations are returned at all -- it does not truncate the must-keep set to fit.
seed_claim.falsification_test: Read project() and confirm must-keep overflow returns INSUFFICIENT_PROJECTION rather than truncating.

setup.task: Given the seeded claim about project()'s must-keep/budget-overflow behavior, walk through, step by step, what would happen if node_budget were set to exactly 0 while the seed set contains at least one active claim. This is a hypothetical walk-through of the mechanism, not something you have actually run or observed happen in this conversation. Commit your conclusion with whatever evidence_class from the required schema most honestly reflects the nature of this reasoning.

admitted_claim.content: With node_budget=0 and ≥1 active seed, must-keep size ≥1 > budget, so project() returns INSUFFICIENT_PROJECTION and emits nothing.
admitted_claim.falsification_test: Execute project(seed_ids=[any_active_claim], node_budget=0) and confirm it returns exactly INSUFFICIENT_PROJECTION with empty result sets.

model_raw_text:
The seeded rule states that must-keep begins with every active seed_id. With node_budget exactly 0 and at least one active seed present, that initial set already has size ≥ 1. The subsequent walk for DEPENDS_ON/CONTRADICTS hinges can only enlarge it. Because size > budget, the rule mandates an immediate INSUFFICIENT_PROJECTION return with no output at all; truncation is explicitly disallowed. The outcome follows by direct logical necessity from the given mechanism.
